note: Physical variable concepts the selector may choose. A product is a fallback only for the same physical quantity (same definition_class, unit and temporal support). Order is decided by observation basis, record length and known defects — never by which trend is larger or more significant.

concepts.label: Precipitation
concepts.description: Water reaching the surface as rain or snow, as a monthly mean rate. It is the supply term of the land water balance and the input of meteorological drought indices such as the SPI. Monthly means describe wet and dry months; they cannot resolve single storms, rain intensity or floods.

quantity_definition.quantity: precipitation rate at the surface (liquid + solid)
quantity_definition.observed_or_modelled: satellite–gauge merged estimates (IMERG, GPCP) or bias-corrected reanalysis (MERRA-2)

concepts.product_order_reason: 1 p_imerg: finest observation-based product (0.1°). 2 p_gpcp: observation-based, longest record (1979), but 2.5° native grid. 3 p_m2: reanalysis (model with observation-based correction), used only when no observation-based product applies. p_m2land is registered but not approved: same model as p_m2 over land, shorter record, never available without p_m2. A recipe that needs a long calibration record (e.g. SPI) must declare it before the product decision, which then skips products whose record is too short.

relative_change.definition: 100 × slope per decade ÷ mean of the fixed seasonal baseline cycle of the selected product in the region
relative_change.caution: A percentage becomes unstable where the baseline mean is close to zero; the original-unit slope is always the primary result.

concepts.label: Evapotranspiration
concepts.description: Water returned from the surface to the atmosphere by soil evaporation, plant transpiration, interception loss and sublimation, as a monthly mean rate. The approved product is the MERRA-2 grid-cell total (a model estimate, including open-water evaporation in coastal and lake cells); evapotranspiration is not measured directly. Land-only evapotranspiration products are a different quantity and are not used as fallbacks.

quantity_definition.quantity: total evaporation / evapotranspiration rate from the surface of the whole grid cell (land and open water)

concepts.product_order_reason: et_m2 only. The concept is ONE physical quantity: the MERRA-2 grid-cell total evaporation (EVAP), which includes open-water evaporation in coastal and lake cells. et_m2land (MERRA-2 land tiles only) and et_gldas (GLDAS Noah land surface model, land only) are land-only evapotranspiration, a different quantity wherever a region contains open water, so they are registered for inspection but are NOT approved fallbacks (spec §6.1: same category is not the same physical quantity). Where et_m2 is not applicable the variable is reported as unavailable; no land-only product is substituted.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: the quantity can be negative or its mean can be close to zero, so slope ÷ mean is not meaningful.

concepts.label: Potential evapotranspiration
concepts.description: Evaporation that would occur from a well-watered surface under the prevailing radiation, temperature, humidity and wind: a measure of atmospheric evaporative demand, not of water actually evaporated.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: the quantity can be negative or its mean can be close to zero, so slope ÷ mean is not meaningful.

concepts.label: Root-zone soil moisture
concepts.description: Water stored in the soil layer that plant roots draw from. It reflects the balance of precipitation, evapotranspiration and drainage over weeks to months and is the quantity agricultural drought refers to. The prepared product is a land surface model estimate without irrigation.

quantity_definition.quantity: soil water storage in the root zone
quantity_definition.depth_or_height: root zone (depth depends on the Noah vegetation class)

relative_change.definition: 100 × slope per decade ÷ mean of the fixed seasonal baseline cycle of the selected product in the region
relative_change.caution: A percentage becomes unstable where the baseline mean is close to zero; the original-unit slope is always the primary result.

concepts.label: Soil moisture, 0–2 m
concepts.description: Water stored in the whole modelled soil column down to 2 m. It changes more slowly than the root zone and is the soil component of terrestrial water storage in the model.

relative_change.definition: 100 × slope per decade ÷ mean of the fixed seasonal baseline cycle of the selected product in the region
relative_change.caution: A percentage becomes unstable where the baseline mean is close to zero; the original-unit slope is always the primary result.

concepts.label: Surface soil moisture, 0–10 cm
concepts.description: Water stored in the top 10 cm of soil. It responds within days to rain and evaporation; the monthly mean describes how wet the surface was on average.

relative_change.definition: 100 × slope per decade ÷ mean of the fixed seasonal baseline cycle of the selected product in the region
relative_change.caution: A percentage becomes unstable where the baseline mean is close to zero; the original-unit slope is always the primary result.

concepts.label: Root-zone soil wetness (degree of saturation)
concepts.description: Degree of saturation of the root zone between 0 (dry) and 1 (saturated) in the MERRA-2 land model. It is a different quantity from soil water storage in millimetres and is not a substitute for it.

quantity_definition.depth_or_height: root zone of the MERRA-2 land model

concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: a bounded fraction; a percentage of a fraction is easily misread as percentage points.

concepts.label: Terrestrial water storage anomaly
concepts.description: Change in the total mass of water on and below the land surface (groundwater, soil moisture, snow, ice, surface water) measured by satellite gravimetry, expressed as equivalent water height relative to the product's own reference mean. It is observed, but only at scales of a few hundred kilometres, and it cannot by itself say which storage component changed.

quantity_definition.quantity: terrestrial water storage anomaly (equivalent water height)

concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: an anomaly has no meaningful mean to divide by.

concepts.label: Runoff
concepts.description: Water leaving the soil column as surface and subsurface runoff in a land model, as a monthly mean rate. It indicates how much water the land generates for rivers; it is not measured river discharge and contains no routing, reservoirs or withdrawals.

quantity_definition.depth_or_height: surface and base of the soil column
quantity_definition.observed_or_modelled: modelled (land surface model / reanalysis land model)

concepts.product_order_reason: 1 runoff (GLDAS Noah, 0.25°): kept as primary so that soil moisture, snow and runoff come from one consistent land model. 2 ro_m2 (MERRA-2 land model). Levels differ strongly between models; products are never spliced.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: the quantity is zero for much of the year or in many regions, so its mean is close to zero.

concepts.label: Snow water equivalent
concepts.description: Depth of water that the snowpack would yield if melted. It describes seasonal water stored as snow. The prepared product is a land surface model estimate and is not valid over glaciers and ice sheets.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: the quantity is zero for much of the year or in many regions, so its mean is close to zero.

concepts.label: Near-surface air temperature
concepts.description: Temperature of the air near the surface, as a monthly mean. It is the usual variable for warming and one of the drivers of evaporative demand and snow melt. Monthly means cannot identify individual hot days or heatwaves.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: °C has an arbitrary zero, so slope ÷ mean is not meaningful.

concepts.label: Land surface temperature (model, all-sky)
concepts.description: Skin temperature of the land surface in a reanalysis land model, averaged over all hours and all sky conditions. A skin temperature differs from air temperature, especially over dry or sparsely vegetated land.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: °C has an arbitrary zero, so slope ÷ mean is not meaningful.

concepts.label: Daytime land surface temperature (satellite, clear-sky)
concepts.description: Skin temperature of the land surface retrieved from thermal infrared at the daytime satellite overpass under clear sky. It is an observation, but samples only cloud-free days at one time of day and is sensitive to overpass-time drift.

quantity_definition.quantity: land surface skin temperature, clear-sky daytime overpass

concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: °C has an arbitrary zero, so slope ÷ mean is not meaningful.

concepts.label: Vapour pressure deficit
concepts.description: Difference between the water vapour the air could hold at its temperature and the water vapour it holds. It measures the drying power of the air on plants and soil and rises with temperature when humidity does not keep pace.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: the mean is close to zero in cold and humid regions.

concepts.label: Surface net radiation
concepts.description: Net shortwave plus net longwave radiation at the land surface: the energy available for evaporation, heating the air and heating the ground.

quantity_definition.quantity: surface net radiation (net shortwave + net longwave)
quantity_definition.observed_or_modelled: modelled (land surface model / reanalysis land model)

concepts.product_order_reason: 1 rn (GLDAS Noah): consistent with the other GLDAS land variables. 2 rn_m2 (MERRA-2 land model).
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: the quantity can be negative or its mean can be close to zero, so slope ÷ mean is not meaningful.

concepts.label: Downward shortwave radiation
concepts.description: Solar radiation reaching the surface. It reflects cloudiness and aerosols as well as the seasonal sun, and is a main driver of evaporative demand and plant growth.

relative_change.definition: 100 × slope per decade ÷ mean of the fixed seasonal baseline cycle of the selected product in the region
relative_change.caution: A percentage becomes unstable where the baseline mean is close to zero; the original-unit slope is always the primary result.

concepts.label: Near-surface wind speed
concepts.description: Speed of the air near the surface, without direction. It affects evaporative demand; it does not describe circulation patterns or storms.

relative_change.definition: 100 × slope per decade ÷ mean of the fixed seasonal baseline cycle of the selected product in the region
relative_change.caution: A percentage becomes unstable where the baseline mean is close to zero; the original-unit slope is always the primary result.

concepts.label: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
concepts.description: Normalised difference vegetation index from satellite reflectance: a dimensionless measure of how green the land surface is. It tracks leaf cover and its seasonality; it is not biomass, crop yield or ecosystem health.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: an index with an arbitrary scale and possible negative values.

concepts.label: Sea surface temperature
concepts.description: Temperature of the ocean surface from a blended satellite and in situ analysis, as a monthly mean. Available for ocean regions only. Monthly means describe ocean warming; they cannot resolve marine heatwave events.
concepts.relative_change_note: No relative change: °C has an arbitrary zero, so slope ÷ mean is not meaningful.
